chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman to whom the death of her husband was announced, so she observed the waiting period and married, then her first husband came and divorced her, and the second one separated from her. How long is her waiting period for the second [husband]? He said: 'Three menstrual periods. And indeed, she purifies her womb only by three menstrual periods, and she becomes permissible to all men.'

Zurarah said: This is because some people said she observes two waiting periods, one from each, but Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) rejected that and said: 'She observes three menstrual periods and becomes permissible to men.'

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.تَسْتَبْرِئُ رَحِمَهَا: She purifies her womb (completes the waiting period to ensure no pregnancy)
key_terms.قُرُوءٍ: Menstrual periods (used as a measure for the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman whose first husband returns after she married a second?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Baqir, the concept of 'istibra'' (purging the womb) is clarified as a single three-month period rather than cumulative waiting periods, resolving the dispute among scholars who argued for two separate iddahs. This establishes that once the three menstrual cycles are completed, the woman is fully purified and permissible to all men, not just the second husband. The hadith highlights the Shia jurisprudential preference for simplicity in marital transitions when the first husband's return is unexpected.
